papers.title: Peptide Bioink: Self-Assembling Nanofibrous Scaffolds for Three-Dimensional Organotypic Cultures
papers.abstract: Printable scaffolds with adequate mechanical strength and stiffness are sought after to ensure viability of printed cells and tissues. We report the first peptide bioinks-lysine-containing hexapeptides that self-assemble into stable, nanofibrous three-dimensional hydrogels with unprecedented stiffness of up to 40 kPa. These biocompatible scaffolds support the three-dimensional culture of human stem cells and differentiation of primary cells into organotypic (gastrointestinal and skin) structures for high-throughput screening, diagnosis, and tissue engineering.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发具有足够机械强度的可打印支架以支持三维细胞培养
summary_zh.method: 设计含赖氨酸的六肽，自组装形成纳米纤维水凝胶
summary_zh.result: 获得刚度高达40 kPa的水凝胶，支持干细胞培养和类器官分化
summary_zh.validation: 体外培养人干细胞和原代细胞，验证生物相容性和组织形成

summary_en.motivation: To develop printable scaffolds with sufficient mechanical properties for 3D cell culture and tissue engineering.
summary_en.method: Designed lysine-containing hexapeptides that self-assemble into nanofibrous hydrogels with tunable stiffness.
summary_en.result: Achieved unprecedented stiffness up to 40 kPa and demonstrated support for human stem cell culture and organotypic differentiation.
summary_en.validation: In vitro culture of human stem cells and primary cells confirmed biocompatibility and formation of gastrointestinal and skin organotypic structures.
